ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A block of mass $M$ and positive charge $Q$ slides down an incline plane at angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal, starting at position $(x_0, y_0)$. The system is exposed to an upward electric field given by $E(y) = \beta(y_{0}- y)$, where $\beta > 0$.

1. (a) Find an expression for $y_e$, the position where the block experiences net zero vertical force.
2. (b) What is the force acting on the block when it is in contact with the incline plane?
3. (c) Once the block has lost contact with the plane it begins to oscillate in the field. What frequency does it oscillate at?

The system is exposed to an upward electric field given by $E(y) = \beta(y_{0}- y)$, where $\beta > 0$. 1. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a block labeled M,Q placed on an inclined plane; the inclined plane slopes downward to the right and makes an angle α with the horizontal line. The coordinate axes in the lower left corner show the x-axis pointing to the right and the y-axis pointing upward. On the right side of the inclined plane, multiple vertically upward arrows are drawn and labeled E(y), indicating that the electric field direction is upward. Reasoning: The problem gives the electric field E(y)=β(y0-y), and the charge Q is positive, so the electric field force is upward, with magnitude QE(y)=Qβ(y0-y). Gravity is vertically downward, with magnitude Mg. (a) When the net vertical force is zero, the upward electric field force equals the downward gravity: Qβ(y0-ye)-Mg=0. Therefore y0-ye=Mg/(βQ), obtaining ye=y0-Mg/(βQ). (b) When the block is still in contact with the inclined plane, the downward equivalent magnitude after combining gravity and the electric field force in the vertical direction is Mg-Qβ(y0-y). Projecting this vertical resultant force along the direction of the inclined plane, the force in the downward-sliding direction is F(y)=[Mg-Qβ(y0-y)]sinα. (c) After leaving the inclined plane, the vertical motion satisfies M y¨=Qβ(y0-y)-Mg. Using the equilibrium position ye satisfying Qβ(y0-ye)-Mg=0, it can be rewritten as M y¨=-Qβ(y-ye). This is simple harmonic motion, with angular frequency ω=sqrt(βQ/M), frequency f=ω/(2π)=1/(2π) sqrt(βQ/M).
